thread:
james_support: Escalation from ACME — invoice spike: 3.2M tokens billed in 2026-03-16 00:00-06:00 UTC window, but our per-route dashboard shows ~1.1M served. Customer insists no traffic increase. Any known prefetched/batcher accounting that could explain a large billed-but-not-served delta?

alyssa_billing: Seen this pattern before with warmup-prefetch. Need meter rows + batch trace id. Can you grab the reconciler export and any batch traces? :eyes:

devon_infra: We rolled continuous-batcher v2 on 2026-03-15 and adjusted prefetch_sizing. Possible this is related. I'll pull batch traces for the window.

mike_repro: To repro quickly: run a short script that simulates many small chat opens with a common prefix so KV prefetch fires. Add X-Client-Id header for customer so traces are obvious.

james_support: Attaching quick meter snippet and a batch trace id we got from customer-side logs: trace=tr_2410506789_abc123. Reconciler rows show a big metered_tokens column but much smaller served_tokens. Snippet below:

```
# meter_export rows (trimmed)
2026-03-16T04:01:12Z trace=tr_2410506789_abc123 metered_tokens=1200000 served_tokens=400000 route=/chat client_id=acme prefetched=false
2026-03-16T04:10:45Z trace=tr_2410506790_abc124 metered_tokens=2000000 served_tokens=700000 route=/chat client_id=acme prefetched=true batcher=ctb-v2
```

devon_infra: I can see prefetched=true in the rows. Current metering treats prefetch token generation as billable at the time of token generation (we charge for tokens produced by the model even if they are only used to warm a KV cache). served_tokens only counts tokens emitted in responses to the client. If a prefetch warms KV and that warmed prefix never gets used (evicted or mismatched), customer gets billed but served stays low.

alyssa_billing: That aligns with why invoice > dashboard. Invoice uses metered_tokens; dashboard's served metric is downstream (post-response) so it misses prefetch. We need to communicate this clearly to ACME and offer mitigation.

mike_repro: Repro steps I used (safe, non-prod):
```bash
# simulate continuous-batcher prefetch warming
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
    -H "X-Client-Id: acme-test" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-v1","prompt":"shared_prefix: lorem ipsum","max_tokens":64}' &
done
wait
# then check reconciler: /internal/meter_export?client_id=acme-test&start=2026-03-16T00:00:00Z&end=2026-03-16T06:00:00Z
```

usage-bot: METRICS_ALERT: ctb-v2 prefetched token rate increased 3.1x between 04:00-04:15 UTC (customer acme-test).

devon_infra: Short-term mitigations:
- ask customer to disable prefetch on their tenant (prefetch_enabled=false) or pin a model variant with smaller prefetch window
- throttle prefetch size (prefetch_sizing -> smaller)
- if they need immediate relief, we can offer a one-off invoice adjustment while we investigate further

alyssa_billing: Action items:
- james_support -> reply to ACME explaining billed vs served difference and share the reconciler snippet + trace id (tr_2410506789_abc123). Suggest disabling prefetch as a mitigation.
- devon_infra -> open eng ticket (ENG-INC-5412) to investigate whether prefetch-generated tokens should be flagged differently in metering or have a policy change for warmup credits.
- mike_repro -> attach repro script and the batch traces to ENG ticket.

james_support: I'll draft the customer message and propose a credit while eng investigates. Draft: "TL;DR: metered tokens include prefetch/warmup requests from our continuous batcher. Those tokens are billable by current policy even if they were not later served to end users. We can disable prefetch or reduce its size to avoid future spikes; we can also review credits for the spike window."

alyssa_billing: Sounds good. Please include recommended statements: why invoice > dashboard, what we can change, and an ETA for eng investigation (ASAP, expect preliminary findings in 48 hours).

devon_infra: I'll start the trace review now and attach logs to ENG-INC-5412. If we confirm a policy bug or double-counting bug, we should prepare a customer-facing KB and consider an automated reconciler that flags big metered_vs_served deltas for billing review.

mike_repro: Uploaded my script + a small set of traces to the ticket. I could reproduce a ~2.8x metered/served ratio locally using ctb-v2 with prefetch_sizing=large.

james_support: Thanks team — i'll message ACME with the mitigation and request permission to disable prefetch on their tenant temporarily. Will update thread when they respond. :wave:
